findings.statement: Apps that access restricted-scope data from or through a third-party server must go through a security assessment from Google-empanelled, independent third-party assessors, standardized via the App Defense Alliance's CASA framework.

Apps using restricted scopes must be reverified and reassessed at least every 12 months after the assessor's Letter of Assessment approval date; adding a new restricted scope not previously covered can also trigger reassessment.

Restricted scope verification can potentially take several weeks to complete; brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days if branding details changed, and a compliant verification result stays valid for only 7 days before it must be published or re-verified.

findings.statement: Verification requires a demonstration video (uploaded to YouTube, set to Unlisted) showing how the granted scopes are used, plus a written explanation of why more limited scopes aren't sufficient.

Unverified apps are capped at 100 new users in total (adjustable based on app history, developer reputation, and risk level); the restriction lasts until verification completes, which can take several months for sensitive data.
Changing your OAuth client, adding new scopes after verification, or changing your product name, redirect URLs, or JavaScript origins can require verifying again.

Gmail scopes fall into three tiers: non-sensitive (e.g. gmail.labels), sensitive (e.g. gmail.send), and restricted (e.g. gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, mail.google.com); an app's overall classification is set by its single most restrictive requested scope.
Google Workspace admins can block installation of unverified third-party apps by default, and can mark a specific app as Trusted to exempt it from that restriction.

findings.statement: Verification isn't required for apps that qualify for an exception: personal use, development/testing/staging projects, service-owned data only, internal organizational use, or domain-wide installation.

claim.text: Registering an app and requesting verification is open to any developer; the security assessment uses a Google-approved third-party assessor you hire, not a Google partnership requirement.
Apps requesting restricted Gmail scopes (like gmail.readonly or gmail.modify) must complete an independent third-party CASA security assessment.
Apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes must complete Google's OAuth verification process.
Google Workspace admins can block unverified third-party apps by default and must mark one Trusted to exempt it.
Unverified apps are capped at 100 new users in total until verification completes.

tierReason.text: Apps requesting restricted Gmail scopes (such as gmail.readonly or gmail.modify) must pass an independent third-party security assessment, standardized on Google's CASA framework, on top of OAuth verification - and must repeat that assessment at least every 12 months.

claim.text: Google's own docs describe restricted-scope verification as potentially taking several weeks to complete.

scopeForks.text: Requesting only non-sensitive or sensitive Gmail scopes (never a restricted one like gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, or mail.google.com) skips the mandatory third-party security assessment - OAuth verification alone is still required, but it's a lighter process. Apps that qualify for an exception (personal use, internal-only, domain-wide installation, etc.) can skip verification entirely.

claim.text: Composio's managed Gmail OAuth app lets a developer connect Gmail without creating their own Google Cloud project, and says it handles verification and the CASA assessment on the developer's behalf.

whatYouLose.text: On a managed app, the consent screen shows the platform's name and brand instead of yours, and scopes and rate limits are typically fixed rather than something you control.

whenToSwitch.text: Switch to your own Google Cloud project once you need your own branding, specific scopes, or direct control over your verification and assessment status.

flow.text: A developer registers an app in Google Cloud Console, requests Gmail scopes, and - depending on scope sensitivity - completes OAuth verification and, for restricted scopes, a third-party security assessment before the unverified-app limits are lifted.
